text:
**My pick: XTAR VC4SL**, for most people. The Nitecore UMS4 is the better choice if you also charge LiFePO4 cells. I only have review and product pages for these, not verified store links, so the links below go to where you can check price and buy.

## Top choices

**XTAR VC4SL (about $32.90)**
- It has 4 independent bays, USB-C input with QC3.0, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A. It takes everything from 10440 to 32650, plus AA/AAA NiMH.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance, and it has capacity-test and storage modes.
- Best-Batteries rates it 4.3/5. Stephen Knight calls it "one of the best USB powered, and consumer chargers available."
- Downsides: it defaults to the highest current (3A), which some cells can't handle, so set it manually. One reviewer saw it mistake NiMH cells for Li-ion and end NiMH charges early, so watch it at the start of a charge. It doesn't list LiFePO4 support.
- Links: [Best-Batteries review and price](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/) and [1Lumen review](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/)

**Nitecore UMS4 (about $38.95)**
- It also has 4 independent bays and USB-C with QC input. It does up to 3A in a single slot, and it supports LiFePO4 and Li-ion restoration.
- Listed protections: reverse polarity, short circuit, overtime charging, and internal resistance/battery health display.
- Links: [Nitecore product page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4) and [price on Best-Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/)

**Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics named it its "best for most people" pick. It has selectable 500mA/1A charging, an LCD for every bay, UL/CE/FCC marks, and 4.6 stars across 4,608 Amazon reviews.
- Caveat: that site earns affiliate commissions, and I have no price or direct link. See the [Smashing Robotics list](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/) for the Amazon link.

## Budget option

**Tenergy TN270 ($18.99)** is a simple 2-bay wall charger at 500 mA per bay, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6-7 hours. Its only listed protections are reverse-polarity detection and status LEDs. It's fine for a flashlight or headlamp, but I'd step up for anything more. [Buy at Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger) (affiliate link).

## Safety tips
- Look for independent bays and a stated termination method. Avoid no-name chargers that don't say how they decide a cell is full.
- Never use a NiMH-only charger on lithium cells.
- A gentler 500mA–1A rate is better for cell life if you're not in a hurry.

Tell me whether you need 2 or 4 bays, USB-C power, or LiFePO4 support and I can narrow this down.
